title: Sales & CS launch kit for Runtime QBatch: demo playflow and enablement collateral
creator: Lena Park
description: Scope: Produce a compact, reproducible enablement kit for Sales and Customer Success to support the runtime-1.20 rollout (QBatch improvements). The kit must enable reps to explain technical benefits, demonstrate value in a 5–8 minute demo, and address common procurement/security questions. This ticket coordinates collateral, release-note copy, demo scripts, recordings, and enablement sessions across PM, Eng, Docs, Design, and GTM.
goals: 1) Make a single-sheet sales brief with measurable claims and linked proof points. 2) Build a repeatable 5–8 minute demo playflow (script + runbook + expected outputs) that works deterministically on hosted and Dedicated. 3) Publish an FAQ oriented to procurement/security + a short objection-handling matrix. 4) Ship a release-notes-ready paragraph and technical appendix for Docs and Marketing.
deliverables:
- Sales one-pager (sell-sheet) with 3 customer-ready value props and a TL;DR metric summary.
- Demo playflow: step-by-step script, terminal/SDK commands, sample input prompts, expected token/latency comparisons, and fallback checklist.
- Objection matrix (top 8 objections + suggested responses and escalation path).
- FAQ (procurement, security, performance, compatibility).
- 25-minute recorded demo + 45-minute live Q&A deck for CS enablement.
- Release notes snippets: short headline, technical appendix, and upgrade considerations for Dedicated/Private customers.
audience_and_stakeholders: Primary: Sales AEs, Solutions Engineers, CS AMs. Secondary: Field Marketing, Growth, Support. Stakeholders: PM (Lena Park), Eng owners (Marco Chen, ENG-7782), Design (Asha Verma), Docs (Raj Patel), Sales Enablement (Maya Thompson), Legal/Security (Olivia Singh).

release_notes_coordination: Coordinate with Docs + Release Engineering to ensure the public release note includes a customer-facing headline and a technical appendix. Sample customer-facing sentence: 'runtime-1.20 introduces QBatch: workload-aware batching that reduces per-token cost by up to 42% on long-turn conversations while preserving 99th percentile latency SLOs.' Technical appendix to include: benchmark harness link, dataset used, hardware config, sequence-length distribution, and quantization profile used in the demo. Docs link placeholder: https://docs.redwood.ai/runtime-1-20/qbatch
demo_playflow_summary: Objective: Show measurable throughput/cost benefits while keeping latency acceptable for interactive demos. Flow: (1) Brief context (30s): why QBatch matters. (2) Live run: two side-by-side runs (baseline model config vs runtime-1.20 with QBatch) on a scripted 3-turn chat with 512 token history. Use SDK streaming response with token latency tracing enabled. (3) Show KV cache warmup + cache-hit scenario. (4) Trigger fallback path (simulate spike) to demonstrate graceful degradation to a smaller model variant. (5) Wrap-up: expected metrics, cost delta, and recommended migration checklist.
demo_commands_and_samples:
- SDK snippet: python quick_demo.py --model gptx-1 --config baseline
- SDK snippet: python quick_demo.py --model gptx-1 --config qbatch-enabled
- Sample prompt set (copy into demo repo): 'user: Summarize the last conversation; assistant: Provide stepwise plan.' (three variants included in demo repo).
- Expected outputs: Show token-per-second, median latency, and percent cost reduction. Benchmarks attached in demo repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-qbatch (placeholder).
success_criteria:
- Sales & CS report they can run the demo reliably in at least 3 of 4 internal test accounts during dry run.
- 70% of SEs rate the kit >= 4/5 for 'closeness to production' after training.
- Assets published in Notion + SFDC with tracking links before GTM live date.
- PR for release notes merged and signed off by Docs and Eng.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Live demo variability due to noisy GPUs or tenant limits. Mitigation: embargoed demo tenants with deterministic seeds + pre-recorded backup video.\nRisk: Security objections about KV cache persistence. Mitigation: security FAQ entry and RSA-approved talking points; escalation path to Security lead.\nRisk: Bench numbers not defensible. Mitigation: include raw harness and metadata in technical appendix and link to reproducible benchmark script.
